architecture.ai_summary:
Liza turns a human goal into reviewed artifacts and integrated code by combining model judgment with deterministic supervision. Initialization binds a committed specification to a project-local YAML blackboard, the shared coordination record, and a declarative delivery pipeline. The selected entry point determines which specification, architecture, coding, and integration stages remain. An orchestrator decomposes work and manages dependencies, while doer/reviewer pairs produce and judge artifacts. Supervisors claim eligible work before launching provider sessions, supply isolated Git worktrees and task-specific prompts, then process submission, revision, approval, and merge outcomes. Structured task outputs carry references into subsequent stages rather than relying on conversation memory. [README.md](README.md) explains the cooperating layers and mode choices; [REPOSITORY.md](REPOSITORY.md) routes readers to operational guides. Pairing uses human gates, while adversarial pairing has a smaller Markdown blackboard workflow. Consult purpose and hints, then stacklit derive, for navigation; this summary adds sequencing, authority boundaries, and consequences of changing behavior.

The key boundary separates agents deciding what satisfies a task from Go code deciding which operations are legal. Agents call CLI commands, including structured --json responses; [ADR-0057](specs/architecture/ADR/0057-mcp-server-removal-cli-native-access-control.md) supersedes the historical built-in MCP server described in ADR-0012. CLI policy checks and typed operations converge on locked blackboard mutations, while provider execution and Git work happen outside that transaction. internal/db/blackboard.go serializes read-modify-write and validates state hygiene before publishing parseable YAML; persistence protection does not substitute for domain validation. internal/ops/agent_authority.go compares a caller's registration generation with current state inside the mutation lock, rejecting stale instances before their writes. The documented supervisor recovery order is handoff, already-owned executing work, then fresh claims. A heartbeat proves supervisor activity, not task progress: a separate watchdog observes task, worktree, and provider-output changes and can block stalled execution. Lease-first recovery preserves ownership across uncertain process namespaces; [supervision-model.md](specs/architecture/supervision-model.md) explains the recovery contract.

Review and integration preserve evidence anchored to commits. internal/ops/submit_review.go checks ownership, executing state, checkpoint presence, task branch, and submitted commit equality with worktree HEAD before rebasing onto integration. Its mechanical test-driven-development gate checks changed test files or a recorded waiver for applicable tasks; it cannot establish that tests were written first or adequately encode intent, which remains reviewer judgment. The pipeline supplies role-pair statuses and review policy, so a new lifecycle state affects eligibility, validation, prompt context, and operator displays together. Merge requires approved state and a review commit; when a worktree is recorded, mismatched HEAD produces INTEGRATION_FAILED. internal/ops/wt_merge.go validates protected artifact references against the candidate tree, constructs commits without checking out integration, and advances the ref using compare-and-swap: update only if the old commit still matches. Post-merge artifact failures or failing integration scripts attempt conditional rollback, preserving later concurrent work. A missing integration script produces a warning and permits progress, so merge success alone does not establish test execution. [INVARIANTS.md](INVARIANTS.md) additionally requires clean integration evidence to name the current integration commit; later mutations invalidate completion tied to an older snapshot.

Provider selection and context delivery extend the same lifecycle. internal/agent/launch_resolver.go gives explicit CLI selection precedence over profile CLI and role/global defaults, merges provider catalog settings with project overrides, and renders executable arguments and prompt transport. Ordinary CLI and acpx-backed sessions share a launch boundary; acpx session names are task-scoped to prevent unrelated tasks accumulating context. Optional structural, symbol, functional, and semantic indexes help agents navigate their assigned repository but do not replace source verification. Formatting changes can remain local when the operation contract stays stable; new provider capabilities may require coordinated activation assets, runtime execution, profile resolution, and identity handling. New pipeline roles likewise need coherent permissions, context sections, transitions, and reviewer expectations. [Architectural issues](specs/architecture/architectural-issues.md) records coupling risks and limitations; verify its dated findings against current code before treating an individual issue as still present. The [decision index](specs/architecture/ADR/README.md) provides historical rationale.

Implementation choices are bounded by repository requirements. go.mod declares Go 1.25.5; Makefile synchronizes embedded assets before normal builds and tests. [GETTING_STARTED.md](GETTING_STARTED.md) supports Linux, macOS, and Windows, with Git Bash requirements on Windows, so process control, paths, and shell execution must retain platform-aware behavior. [GUARDRAILS.md](GUARDRAILS.md) G1.1 requires runtime behavior to remain stack-agnostic: target-project build and setup commands must come from configuration or supported detection rather than this repository's Go tooling. G1.3 requires presentation through centralized branding and rendered assets, retaining structural import identities and documented compatibility exceptions. internal/brand/brand.go prefers nonempty branded environment values over legacy LIZA aliases, so the hint names describe the default brand. README.md identifies Apache 2.0 licensing. REPOSITORY.md explains master versus generated assets, while INVARIANTS.md provides the protection matrix to consult before evolving state, concurrency, review, or integration behavior.
